title: map, filter, reduce, and chaining
hook: map transforms each element, filter keeps some, reduce folds the array into one value — chained together they replace most explicit for-loops with declarative pipelines that interviewers expect you to implement from scratch.

blocks.text: **Array.prototype.map** returns new array of same length with transformed elements. **filter** returns subset passing predicate. **reduce** accumulates left-to-right with `(acc, cur, index, array) =>` — initial value optional but recommended. **Chaining**: `arr.filter().map().reduce()`. All are **non-mutating** on source array (unless you mutate inside callback). **Sparse arrays**: map/filter skip holes; reduce may treat holes differently — know spec.

entries.plainDefinition: Transform each element — 1:1 length output array.
Keep elements where predicate returns truthy.
Fold array to single value — sum, group, max, compose pipeline.
JS array methods are eager — each pass allocates. Generators/LINQ lazy differ.
entries.example: map then filter scans twice — fuse in one loop for perf if needed.

blocks.text: Daily data transforms in frontend and Node — DTO mapping, totals, grouping. Interviews: implement map/filter/reduce without built-ins; discuss O(n) chain vs single loop. C# **LINQ Select/Where/Aggregate** is lazy on IEnumerable; JS array methods **always eager** and allocate intermediate arrays.

blocks.title: Interview trap: reduce without initial value
blocks.body: Empty array reduce without initial throws TypeError. On non-empty, first element becomes acc — risky for sum types. Always pass initial value in production.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Mutating acc or source elements inside callbacks unexpectedly. reduce without initial on possibly empty arrays. map when forEach was intended (ignoring return). Chaining three passes on huge arrays without profiling.

blocks.text: Implement map/filter/reduce yourself for interviews. Fuse loops when hot path.allocation matters. **async** in map does not await — use for...of or Promise.all(arr.map(async ...)). **Object.groupBy** (ES2024) replaces some reduce grouping. Big-O still O(n) per pass — chain of k passes is O(kn).

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot implement map from scratch. Using async callback in map expecting sequential await. Unaware empty reduce throws without seed.

interviewTakeaways: map/filter return new arrays; reduce folds to one value.
Always pass reduce initial value for empty-safe code.
JS chain is eager — LINQ IEnumerable is lazy until terminal.
60s: map transform, filter subset, reduce aggregate. Chain for clarity. Implement from scratch in interviews. async map needs Promise.all. C# Select/Where/Aggregate.
Follow-up: groupBy with reduce vs Object.groupBy.
commonPitfalls: reduce without initial on arrays that may be empty.
async map without Promise.all — concurrent not sequential confusion.
Strong answer: implement map/filter/reduce, eager vs lazy LINQ, always seed reduce.
